lines.text: Factorise fully → take out the HCF of the numbers and the lowest power of each shared letter, then expand to check ({{lesson:2.2}})
Unknown in the power, such as $5^{x} = 125$ → write both sides as powers of the same base, then set the indices equal ({{lesson:2.4}})
Two linear equations with two unknowns → make one coefficient the same size in both, then subtract (same signs) or add (different signs) ({{lesson:2.5}})
List the integers that satisfy an inequality → sketch a number line; include an end only if it is an integer with $\leqslant$ or $\geqslant$ ({{lesson:2.6}})
nth term when the terms go up or down by the same amount $d$ → $dn + (a - d)$, where $a$ is the first term and $a - d$ the term before it ({{lesson:2.7}})
Solve an equation from a drawn graph → for $\ldots = 0$ read where the curve crosses the $x$-axis; for $\ldots = k$ draw $y = k$ and read the $x$-values where it meets the curve ({{lesson:2.10}})
Quadratic equation → rearrange to $\ldots = 0$ and factorise; if it won't factorise, or the answer must be to 2 d.p. or in surd form, use the quadratic formula or complete the square ({{lesson:2.5}})
One linear and one non-linear equation → substitute the linear one into the other, solve the quadratic, then give the answers in pairs ({{lesson:2.5}})
$y$ proportional, or inversely proportional, to a power or root of $x$ → write $y = kx^{n}$ or $y = \frac{k}{x^{n}}$, find $k$ from the given pair, then substitute ({{lesson:2.8}})
Distance travelled from a speed–time graph → area under the graph, split at each corner into rectangles, triangles and trapezia ({{lesson:2.9}})
Turning point of a quadratic without calculus → complete the square: $(x + p)^{2} + q$ has minimum point $(-p, q)$ ({{lesson:2.11}})

Stationary points of a curve → solve $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$ and substitute each $x$ into the curve for $y$; $\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}} < 0$ is a maximum, $> 0$ a minimum ({{lesson:2.12}})
